restaurants.name: Pujol
restaurants.generatedDescription: Pujol is a renowned dining establishment located in Polanco, known for its upscale ambiance and exquisite cuisine. Since its opening in 2000, the restaurant has been a prominent figure in the fine dining scene, earning two Michelin stars. Chef-owner Enrique Olvera has skillfully elevated traditional Mexican dishes such as mole, infusing them with historical and cultural significance.
restaurants.address: Tennyson 133, Polanco, Polanco IV Secc, Miguel Hidalgo, 11570 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Pujol in Mexico City is a stunning and exceptional dining experience, deserving of its 2 Michelin stars. Reviewers praise the top-class food that exemplifies craft, skill, and showcases Mexican ingredients like mole in a complex yet delicious way. The octopus tacos and tostada de quelites stand out among creative and delicious courses. Service is exceptional with multilingual staff providing detailed explanations of dishes. The elegant decor creates a tranquil atmosphere for an immersive dining experience, though some mention the meal duration can be lengthy. Overall, Pujol offers incredible flavors, impeccable service, and beautiful surroundings that make it a must-visit for food enthusiasts seeking an extraordinary culinary adventure.
reasonsToVisit: Experience exceptional Michelin-starred Mexican cuisine at its finest
Enjoy creative dishes showcasing traditional ingredients like mole in innovative ways
Immerse yourself in an elegant Japanese-inspired decor creating a tranquil atmosphere
Indulge in top-notch service with attentive staff offering detailed explanations of each dish
tips: Make reservations well in advance as Pujol tends to book up quickly
Consider opting for the taco tasting menu which receives high praise from reviewers
Be prepared for a leisurely dining experience as meals can stretch over two hours or more
If you have dietary preferences or restrictions, inform the restaurant beforehand for personalized options
Visit during off-peak hours or weekdays for a quieter ambiance and potentially faster service

reviews.reviewText: What a wonderful experience! The food was amazing, the staff were super friendly and helpful, and the atmosphere is beautiful! I want to give the restaurant extra kudos as they were super accommodating for our dietary restrictions. They went all out to make sure they were serving us food that we were able to eat. We had the omakase bar experience and really enjoyed all the food. The tostada was great! I also enjoyed all the sauces and toppings. They made sure that our experience was amazing and it was. Wonderful!!

Unforgettable unique experience that worth the cost. Fixed menu with a selection of mostly two positions. I don’t like and don’t eat Mexican food, but it was so high end and sophisticated, i tried and ate everything apart from some aged sauces We ordered pairing of drinks with food Tried some Mexican sake and Mexican sparkling wine (would not think those exist in general) Desserts were delicious! So unique and not too sweet. Every position was so flavourful, delicious and aesthetically pleasant Must do once in a lifetime! 10/10

Expectations are high for Pujol and they really deliver. The food is amazing - beautifully presented and intriguingly unique. We went for lunch (you must reserve in advance) and they offer set menus with two options (+ a veggie one for main course). Cocktails are yummy. Large and pricey wine list. As for quantity of food, we were full but not stuffed which is perfect. Very pleasant wait staff and excellent Somm. Just note that it’s an indoor/outdoor space so in cold weather it is cold inside (they can give you a blanket so you are comfortable)

Pujol was an absolutely unique experience. From the moment we arrived, we were greeted by our family name (when you reserve, you can upload a photo) by friendly, smiling staff. We were first taken to a bar beneath the branches of a large tree, where we enjoyed water and cocktails while waiting for our table. Once inside, the servers walked us through the five-course menu and gave us time to decide. The menu was inspired by southeastern Mexico, with a strong influence from the state of Chiapas. As each dish was served, every ingredient was explained in great detail—something we truly appreciated. In addition to the five courses, we were treated to delicious appetizers and a slice of strawberry cake wrapped in a banana leaf. We tried the corn with cream and chili, lobster cold soup, grilled octopus, the iconic mole sauces, and wagyu beef. The perfect ending: a chocolate cake topped with ice cream and assorted chocolate bites. Located in Polanco, one of the most exclusive areas in Mexico City, this is truly a once-in-a-lifetime culinary experience.

We had a wonderful experience at Pujol—another check off our bucket list. The food was outstanding, easily some of the best we’ve ever had. Every dish was beautifully presented and thoughtfully executed, with flavors that were bold, eclectic, and memorable. The staff were warm, professional, and attentive without ever making us feel rushed; everything flowed seamlessly from start to finish. A highlight was being invited to tour the kitchen and see the entire operation in action, which added an extra layer of appreciation for the care and precision behind the scenes. Overall, it was a truly memorable experience, and both the food and service fully live up to the restaurant’s reputation. Very well deserving of its two Michelin stars. Muchas gracias!

restaurants.name: Quintonil
restaurants.description: Noted restaurant with a tasting menu offering ambitious meat & seafood dishes, plus wine pairing.
restaurants.generatedDescription: Quintonil is a renowned restaurant in Polanco, offering a tasting menu that features ambitious meat and seafood dishes paired with wines. It has been recognized as one of the top Mexican restaurants, serving elevated versions of traditional Mexican cuisine such as intense mole sauce, tostadas, grilled meats, and soups infused with authentic ingredients like escamoles, chapulines, amaranth, maize, mamey, and soursop.
restaurants.address: Av. Isaac Newton 55, Polanco, Polanco IV Secc, Miguel Hidalgo, 11560 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Quintonil is described as a theatrical experience that leaves diners satiated and chilled, akin to installation art hitting all the senses. The staff is professional yet friendly, offering exceptional service. The innovative menu showcases Mexican culinary traditions with modern techniques and artistic presentation, resulting in breath-taking dishes. While some found the desserts lacking, overall Quintonil delivers an unforgettable dining adventure with impeccable service and a sophisticated ambiance.
reasonsToVisit: Experience a theatrical dining adventure that hits all the senses
Innovative menu showcasing Mexican culinary traditions with modern flair
Impeccable service from knowledgeable and passionate staff
Sophisticated yet welcoming ambiance for an elevated dining experience
tips: Consider booking the countertop experience to watch chefs at work for an immersive dining experience
Be open to trying unique ingredients like insects for an authentic taste of Mexican cuisine
Check prices before ordering as some items can be expensive; clarify costs upfront to avoid surprises
Prepare for a long evening as the dinner experience can take over three hours

reviews.reviewText: Honestly the best michelin experience I have had so far. The bar experience is really fun and each of the dishes was amazing in a different way. Especially the aged beef with mole. The staff members look after everyone so well and have a laugh with you. They even changed the menu for a pregnant lady next to me really well who couldn't eat seafood and she still had amazing dishes. I massively disagree with any other reviews saying service is bad. Also loved their house cocktail and thought the non alcoholic pairing matched each dish incredibly. Was only disappointed by not getting a photo with the Director who left but I wouldn't hesitate to reccomend this to anyone if you want a memory for a lifetime

This establishment is the reason why I love this industry so much. There is significant innovation, fantastic staff, and impressive skill on display. I sat at the bar, which features stunning green marble, and the wait staff gradually introduced themselves. They all wore smiles and genuinely seemed interested in meeting and interacting with every guest. The cooking quality is exceptional, utilising top-notch ingredients sourced from around the country, paired with perfectly chosen wines. The satisfying melt-in-the-mouth texture of the trout lingers in my memory a week after my visit. I found the use of bugs in the dishes to be an enjoyable and inspiring idea. The tomato salad was incredible; the use of textures and fermented ingredients was exactly on point. The standouts keep going, but I will keep the rest a surprise. However, I do have some critiques. The beef, while fantastic, was somewhat overwhelmed by the mole. Although the mole was delicious, it distracted from the key components of the dish. Additionally, the beignet, though tasty, was a bit greasy; a higher oil temperature during frying could enhance the texture. I understand why this place ranks third in the world - keep up the great work!

Lunch at Quintonil was a thoroughly delightful experience, from the warm welcome by the staff to the final petit four. The dishes were creatively composed and offered an impressive glimpse into the diversity of Mexican cuisine. My personal highlight was the smoked trout served with a Cocopache marinade – had I known beforehand what Cocopache are, I probably wouldn’t have eaten it. Fortunately, I didn’t, because the dish was outstanding. The presentation of the various “seasoning elements” is also extremely charming and adds beautifully to the overall experience. A lunch that doesn’t just satisfy, but sparks curiosity – for flavors, for traditions, and for everything Mexican cuisine has to tell beyond the clichés.

Great experience! Delicious food and cocktails; however, the cocktails are not exceptional for a two-star. Some dishes are basic for top-tier restaurants, but still balanced and tasty. More interactive presentations are the thing they should add for the future

Going to Quintonil in Mexico City feels less like a dinner and more like a carefully choreographed sensory experience. The tasting menu moves with intention, each course rooted in Mexican tradition but elevated with modern finesse. The service is warm and precise without being pretentious, the pacing however can afford to slow down a bit. An essential Mexico City experience, for anyone who loves exploring global fine dining.

restaurants.name: Contramar
restaurants.description: Seasonal fish & seafood specialties in a long-running, palapa-style restaurant open since 1998.
restaurants.generatedDescription: Contramar is a renowned seafood restaurant in Mexico City, founded by Gabriela Camara. The establishment has gained widespread acclaim and is a must-visit dining spot for locals and tourists alike. The airy dining room and expansive plant-filled patio provide an inviting ambiance for patrons.
restaurants.address: Durango 200, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Contramar in Mexico City is a bustling seafood haven where the host efficiently manages seating, and the wait staff offers excellent suggestions. Dishes like the tuna tostada stand out for their freshness and flavor, while other plates like the whole fish are well-prepared. Some reviewers found certain dishes just okay but highlighted favorites such as the guacamole and tortillas. The atmosphere is praised, with friendly service and unique seasonings making every dish memorable.
reasonsToVisit: Experience fresh and flavorful seafood dishes like the renowned tuna tostada
Enjoy a lively atmosphere with attentive service at this popular spot in Mexico City
Try unique menu items such as grilled whole fish, soft shell crab, and strawberry meringue
tips: Make a reservation or arrive before 1 pm to avoid long waits
Consider ordering 'half orders' if you plan on trying multiple dishes
Check with staff for weights when ordering items like grilled whole fish

reviews.reviewText: Ordered 2 tuna uni toastada, ceviche, green clam soup, raw shrimps, hibiscus juice, sparkling water. Tuna uni toastada was very good. Tasted a bit like a Japanese food. Ceviche was our favourite, very fresh, they said the seafood arrived today. Green clam soup was also good but I tasted some dirt / grit, maybe the clams weren’t cleaned thoroughly. The raw shrimps were big but tasted just ok (this one we regret ordering it). Hibiscus juice was good, very refreshing. Staff were very friendly. It’s a bit noisy but you can still talk and has a good atmosphere. The total came to around mx $2200 for two people.

Absolutely Exceptional — A Must-Visit in CDMX! Contramar is, without a doubt, the best seafood restaurant I’ve ever been to. Every detail — from the food to the service to the atmosphere — was simply outstanding. The dishes were incredibly fresh and full of flavor, each one crafted with care and attention to detail. The staff was warm, professional, and made us feel genuinely welcomed, adding to the overall experience. The lively yet relaxed ambiance captures the essence of Mexico City perfectly — energetic, elegant, and full of life. Whether you’re a local or visiting, Contramar is a must-visit spot that sets the bar for what a truly great dining experience should be.

It’s worth the hype. This is my second visit and I was so pleased! Reservations online seem to open up 1 month in advance and we had Lady Luck on our side because we walked in right at noon and we were able to snag a table for 2 in full restaurant. Atmosphere is vibrant and servers were exceptional. Classic lunch order: ceviche contramar & pescado a la talla (1kg for 2 people). The ceviche was light and perfectly “cooked” and seasoned. The fish came with corn tortillas and black refried beans and the server prepared the first tacos for us. Drinks: Mescalita (hibiscus + mezcal + black salt rim) & Guava Margarita (perfection without being too sweet. The desserts looked amazing but we were too stuffed!

I can understand why this place is always packed. Good fresh seafood and amazing service. We had seafood soup, tuna tostadas, octopus and potatoes and the half and half sauced dish. All were delicious. Would definetely go there again if I visit CDMX again.

We had an incredible meal at Contramar today — truly one of those long, lazy Mexico City lunches that feels like a full experience. We ordered the holy trinity: the tostadas de atún, the pulpo a la gallega, and the pescado a la talla, and every single dish delivered. The tuna tostadas were bright, crisp, and silky — the kind of bite that makes you stop talking for a second. The pulpo was beautifully tender and smoky. And the pescado a la talla (we did 700g on our server’s recommendation) was the star: perfectly grilled, half red and half green, with enough depth and acidity to keep you chasing every last piece. The energy here is exactly what you want in Roma Norte — vibrant, buzzy, and effortlessly stylish. Perfect for sharing everything and lingering over food and conversation. Highly recommend.

restaurants.name: Restaurante Rosetta
restaurants.description: Acclaimed restaurant serving elevated cuisine with a focus on seasonal and sustainable ingredients.
restaurants.generatedDescription: Restaurante Rosetta, located in the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood of Mexico City, is a renowned dining spot that offers a unique blend of Mexican and Italian-inspired cuisine. The restaurant prides itself on using seasonal and sustainable ingredients to create elevated dishes, such as the pink mole made from beets and shiso. Housed in a beautiful historic mansion with high ceilings and lush greenery, the ambiance alone makes it worth a visit.
restaurants.address: Colima 166, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Restaurante Rosetta offers a mix of experiences according to reviewers. While some found the food disappointing for the price, others were impressed by the fantastic variety of dishes and vegetarian options. The atmosphere is highlighted as cool and perfect for photos, with an upstairs bar described as dreamy. Service receives mixed reviews, with some praising it as excellent while others find room for improvement. The restaurant's setting in a historic mansion adorned with greenery adds to its charm, but opinions vary on whether it truly matches Michelin star standards.
reasonsToVisit: Experience Mexican food with European influences
Enjoy a stunning atmosphere ideal for photos
Try unique dishes like tamales wrapped in corn husks and minestrone soup
Visit one of the top 50 restaurants globally
tips: Make reservations in advance to secure a table
Consider visiting during quieter hours like late evening for a more relaxed experience
Explore the bakery instead if looking for more affordable yet fantastic options
Ask about unique wine selections like orange wines from Baja California

reviews.reviewText: TLDR; this is my first Michelin star restaurant and I would go again. I was wary of my options as a vegetarian since their menu changes so often but Rosetta is an absolute gem. Everything is made with so much care and attention, and surprisingly they have the ability to change your mind about ingredients that you were sure you didn’t like. We arrived early (30 min before they even opened!) and they kindly let us wait in their saloon upstairs and get drinks. The fennel tarralli that comes with the drinks is literally the best bar snack I’ve ever had. Their drinks are also absolutely to die for. Between the two of us, we ordered savoy cabbage tacos (so good we ordered a second), corn tamales, quelites tamal with poblano and mushrooms, flat iron steak and the almond and rose cake. Everything was spectacular. My partner claims it’s the best steak he’s ever had. This is a place that o genuinely feel was worth the money.

The experience inside the restaurant truly lives up to its reputation: the food is exceptional, creative, and executed with precision, and the service is warm, attentive, and genuinely world-class. A special mention goes to my waiter, Osvaldo, who was outstanding. His attention, professionalism, and deep knowledge of the menu elevated the entire experience. Every suggestion he made—from dishes to pairings—was absolutely on point and contributed to an unforgettable meal. His wine recommendation was perfect! My only critique is about the “terrace” seating. When making the reservation, the terrace sounded like an elevated or dedicated outdoor dining area. However, upon arrival, I discovered that the terrace is essentially an extension built onto the sidewalk/street. While many restaurants in Mexico City use similar setups, it contrasts with the expectations one might have for a restaurant of this caliber. For guests expecting a refined terrace environment, this could be surprising or even disappointing. To their credit, when I asked to be moved indoors, the staff was extremely kind and immediately accommodated me, and the indoor atmosphere was everything I hoped for—beautiful, elegant, and fully aligned with the restaurant’s high standards. Overall, with world-class cuisine, exceptional service, and standout team members like Osvaldo, the restaurant is absolutely worth visiting. I would simply recommend that future guests be made aware that the terrace is located on the sidewalk/street so expectations are clear. Will definitely be back. Cheers!!

Last night in CDMX, we were lucky enough to get a last minute resy here. We enjoyed the scallop soursop and avocado leaf. The acidity from soursop makes the texture and freshness of the scallop stands out more. Their sweet potato tortellini comes with a smoky and milky soup base. A very interesting flavor combo. The chicken liver in the pappardelle is tender, juicy and not overcooked. Nothing stands out from their short rib. The tomatillos salad come with a sweet and soy sauce-heavy chile meco. The real highlights from this dinner are actually the two desserts - pear, elderflower and tarragon ice cream and Hoja Santa and white cacao criollo. The former comes with a super balanced flavor. The later comes with a unique presentation and crispy texture. Overall, a overhyped restaurant with Michelin plates and a beautiful setting, but not super impressive in terms of food and flavor.

Restaurant Rosetta which we made reservations to 3 months in advance, is every bit as beautiful as its reputation suggests. A grand, upmarket space with gorgeous high ceilings, lush greenery and art-covered walls that make the dining room feel like a sophisticated indoor garden. The atmosphere is elegant and it fits its Michelin-star status perfectly, from the setting to the service. The specials change daily and is printed fresh; we actually had to wait about ten minutes for that day’s menu to be run off before our server could present it, which only added to the sense that everything is seasonal and very considered. Cocktails were excellent tart, balanced, complex and the kind you want to linger over while you decide what to eat. We started with sourdough rye and ant butter, which was intriguing and fun to try, though there weren’t quite enough ants to really cut through the rich, creamy butter as much as we’d hoped. The short rib with polenta, slow-cooked overnight, was beautifully done and the meat just fell off the bone and melted into the velvety polenta. We enjoyed the roasted suckling pig with sweet potato purée and achiote sauce and the presentation was gorgeous. The runaway star of the meal, though, was the chicken liver pasta: deeply savoury, silky and utterly addictive. We are still somewhat annoyed and delighted that we didn’t stop to photograph it, because we basically devoured it the moment it landed on the table. For dessert, the panna cotta was the jiggliest we’ve ever seen, with that perfect wobble that makes you grin before the first spoonful. Overall, Rosetta feels like a special-occasion restaurant that absolutely earns its Michelin recognition . Gorgeous, green and artful as a space, with food and drinks that are thoughtful, delicious and memorable.

I honestly disagree with many of the 1-star reviews. Even if a Michelin-starred restaurant doesn’t completely exceed someone’s expectations, giving it 1 star feels neither fair nor accurate. The food was genuinely delicious: every dish was incredibly smooth, thoughtfully prepared, and beautifully presented. The pricing was also very reasonable for a Michelin-star restaurant, which made it easy (and worthwhile) to try multiple items. What really stood out was the service. The staff were attentive and thoughtful, even offering to split two dishes half-and-half at half the price so we could try both. That level of hospitality made the experience even better. Overall, a great dining experience and absolutely worth trying.

restaurants.name: Máximo
restaurants.description: Brunch options & tasting menus, including tacos, ceviche & suckling pig, paired with Mexican wines.
restaurants.generatedDescription: Maximo Bistrot is a renowned restaurant known for its brunch options and tasting menus, featuring a variety of dishes such as tacos, ceviche, and suckling pig paired with Mexican wines. Chef Eduardo Lalo Garcia has gained recognition for his culinary skills and dedication to showcasing Mexican ingredients from local farms. The restaurant's vibrant atmosphere is complemented by a colorful emoji mural, creating a casual-chic setting for diners to enjoy the creative and flavorful small plates.
restaurants.address: Av. Álvaro Obregón 65 Bis, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Máximo is a highly acclaimed fine dining restaurant in Mexico City that offers exceptional culinary experiences. Reviewers praise the attentive staff, creative and decadent tasting menus, delicious food with unique flavors, and special non-alcoholic drinks. While some find it expensive, others believe it's worth every penny for the quality of dishes like lamb birria taco and quail. The atmosphere is described as elegant and warm, matching the generous portions served at this legendary spot.
reasonsToVisit: Experience exceptional fine dining with creative and decadent tasting menus
Enjoy delicious food with unique flavors like lamb birria taco and quail
Savor special non-alcoholic drinks crafted by skilled mixologists
Appreciate the elegant and warm atmosphere in a beautiful semi-open space
tips: Make reservations in advance to secure a table at this popular spot
Consider trying the seasonal dishes like cauliflower soup and rib eye recommended by reviewers
Be prepared for potentially slow service even with a reservation
Come hungry to enjoy generous portions of well-executed dishes

reviews.reviewText: One of the best meals I've ever had! The restaurant is beautiful. The food is just as beautiful and delicious. The clarified mango cocktail was amazing. The octopus ceviche was some of the best octopus I've ever had. The blue cheese salad was THE BEST salad I have ever had! The lengua with mole for my main was easily the most tender lengua I have had and the mole elevated it to a completely completely different level. Definitely likely to be the best meal we'll have in CDMX.

Ordered the tasting menu and it was good overall. The wagyu steak and the sorbet ice cream were amazing. The lobster and caviar in toastada were fresh and tasted good. The white fish was very soft and cooked well. The abalone in the soup was great as well, not hard at all and soft to chew. All the ingredients tasted super fresh and high quality. My favourite was the roasted eggplant dip (not part of tasting menu).

An absolutely delightful experience dining at Maximo. The food and ambiance were fantastic However, the thing that stood out the most to us was the level of service they provided. We will definitely be visiting every time we are in Mexico City and speaking about the restaurant to all our peers. We do recommend trying the following menu items: our absolute favourite flavours and textures we found in 1) the Taglietelle oxtail beef ragout and 2) a dessert item - the tarte Tatin. (Both in photos)

The service was very attentive and professional. The menu seemed to offer a wide variety of flavors and styles without being overwhelming. I can’t believe I ordered a cheeseburger, but it was the best one I have ever had in my life. Wines were very reasonable, and the cocktail menu was inventive. We had the onion, ham and guacamole as appetizers. The red snapper and beef tongue was proclaimed by the others to be amazing. The vibe of the restaurant was upscale and avant-garde without being stuffy.

WOW, this was a special, well crafted and tasty lunch. One of the best I experienced in CDMX. I had roasted beets, organic apple vinaigrette, celaya goats cheese & white grapefruit, then red wine braised chicken & parmesan risotto, and finished with chaurand goats cheese ice cream, phyllo, guava & olive oil. They also served the sour dough with eggplant ash, goats cheese, garlic & olive oil spread. The restaurant looks great, has a relaxed but professional vibe and the staff were very welcoming.

restaurants.name: Masala y Maíz
restaurants.description: Trendy spot with an industrial-chic vibe serving traditional meals with Indian & African elements.
restaurants.generatedDescription: Masala y Maíz is a trendy restaurant with an industrial-chic atmosphere that offers traditional dishes infused with Indian and African influences. Located in Colonia Juarez, it is owned by chef duo Norma Listman and Saqib Keval. The menu features a fusion of Mexican, Indian, and East African flavors, such as tetela with duck confit and mole, esquites made with coconut milk and served with chile mayo, and freshly baked doughnuts for dessert.
restaurants.address: C. Artículo 123 116, Colonia Centro, Centro, Cuauhtémoc, 06040 Cuauhtémoc, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Masala y Maíz is a unique culinary gem in Mexico City that blends South Asian, East African, and Mexican flavors into something truly special. While some reviewers found the fusion of Indian & African flavors to be hit or miss, others praised the attentive service and unique dishes like samosas and shrimp. The ambiance received mixed reviews with some mentioning loud noise levels and coldness from staff. However, standout items like the shrimp dish were highly recommended. Overall, Masala y Maíz offers bold and creative dishes that are both familiar and new, with fresh ingredients and thoughtful presentation.
reasonsToVisit: Experience a unique blend of South Asian, East African, and Mexican flavors
Enjoy attentive service with friendly servers who guide you through the menu
Try standout dishes like samosas and shrimp that offer a mix of traditional tastes with innovative twists
tips: Make reservations well in advance due to high demand
Consider letting the waiter pick dishes for you for a fantastic dining experience
Embrace eating with your hands as encouraged by the restaurant's culture

reviews.reviewText: The food was amazing here. The whole experience was amazing. The interior of the restaurant is unique and the service was very good. Our server told us the history of the menu and the restaurant and deeply explained every dish. All the dishes were presented beautifully and the flavors were awesome. I was impressed by every dish especially the chocolate tamale and the chicken. We loved the coasters so much that we asked for clean ones to take home. You must go here if in Mexico City.

Fully stunning food - we had the ceviche, infladita, watermelon salad, prawns, mussels and Chile releno. Everything was beyond amazing but we most loved the prawns (really genre bending) and the mussels. I have to note the fantastic service, Izabela was friendly and amazing at anticipating our every need with great cocktail and wine suggestions. Easily top 5 meals of our life.

We had a wonderful dinner here. The food was absolutely delicious. The meat samsa was especially impressive. We also loved the shrimp, the mussels, and the chicken, which honestly stole the show. Everything was cooked beautifully and tasted amazing. The kitchen overall is fantastic, high-quality. The only downside was the noise level. We were there around 6 pm, and it was so loud that we had to raise our voices to talk. Maybe lowering the music a bit would help, or perhaps the rooms on the right or left side offer better acoustics, since we were seated in the center. Still, the experience and the food were outstanding, and we’d definitely come back.

Masala & Malz is an absolute standout. The food is bursting with flavor, perfectly balanced, and clearly made with care and high-quality ingredients. Every dish we tried was delicious, from the spices to the presentation. The menu is creative while still honoring classic flavors, and everything tasted fresh and authentic. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the service was attentive without being overbearing. You can tell this is a place run by people who genuinely care about the experience they’re delivering. Whether you’re going for a full meal or just drinks and small plates, Masala & Malz is a must-visit and easily one of the best dining experiences we’ve had.

Masala y Maíz continues to be outstanding. The new location is larger, more modern, and still warm. It’s Michelin-recognized two years running, and it shows. Front-of-house service was exceptional—coordinated, attentive, and confident. We had multiple dietary restrictions, and the team handled everything flawlessly, even having the chef guide our coursed meal. Every dish was excellent, with a smart blend of Indian and Mexican flavors. Pricey, but justified. Reservations and a deposit are required. Truly Michelin-level.

restaurants.name: Em
restaurants.generatedDescription: In the Cuauhtemoc neighborhood of Mexico City, Em is a highly anticipated restaurant offering a Japanese-inspired tasting menu. The central dining bar provides an up-close view of chefs preparing dishes like a unique Mexican twist on the traditional Japanese temaki hand roll, featuring local ingredients such as squash blossoms and cotija cheese. The restaurant's elegant design and marble U-shaped dining counter create an inviting atmosphere for guests to enjoy the seasonally driven menu with Japanese influences.
restaurants.address: Tonalá 133, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Em is a highly acclaimed fine dining restaurant in Mexico City that offers an impeccable tasting menu experience. Reviewers praise the articulate attention to detail in every dish, the enjoyable and unique flavors, and the technically prepared meals. The staff is described as warm and attentive, providing excellent service. Guests highlight standout dishes like bunuelo with plantain cream topped with caviar, huitlacoche Chawan mushi, tuna crudo, sea bass, and more. The atmosphere is commended for its New York vibes and well-designed kitchen bar where diners can spectate food preparation led by Chef Jael.
reasonsToVisit: Experience an impeccable fine dining tasting menu with innovative Mexican cuisine infused with Japanese influences
Enjoy unique dishes like bunuelo with plantain cream topped with caviar, huitlacoche Chawan mushi, tuna crudo, sea bass
Witness food preparation at the well-designed kitchen bar led by Chef Jael
tips: Make prepaid reservations via Tock up to two months in advance to secure your spot at this popular restaurant
Request a seat at the central dining bar to watch chefs prepare dishes for a more interactive experience
Try out various hand foods incorporated into their dishes for a fun eating experience

reviews.reviewText: Booked the 4pm seating last minute and ended up the only table. So we got the opportunity to sit at the kitchen counter and watch the magic happen while chatting with the chefs. This was hands down the best dinner experience of the trip. This lucky coincidence helped, but even without it, I honestly found the food more inspiring and tasty than what I ate at Pujol.

This was the best dining experience we had in Mexico City while visiting from Coeur d’Alene Idaho. The corn dish and crab dish are our most memorable courses. We will be trying your additional restaurant concepts. Thank you for an amazing experience!

Beautiful presentation and creative starters, especially the baby corn and the bluefin tuna with avocado. The chawanmushi-style mushroom soup was rich and flavorful. Desserts, especially the Swiss roll, were well balanced and not too sweet. However, the main courses like the steak were underwhelming for the price. Overall tasty but overpriced at around 3700 MXN per person — mainly caters to tourists. Also very crowded

TL;DR: Em was better than the 2 star restaurant I visited in Mexico City. One of the main reasons I’m coming back so soon is to bring my husband here so he can try some of the best food I’ve had in Mexico City. I came to Em with one of my best friends during our girls trip celebrating my bachelorette, and the entire experience was impressive and honestly unforgettable. The food was innovative, thoughtful, and beautifully crafted—every dish felt like it had a purpose. The wine pairing flowed perfectly with the progression of the menu and just elevated everything. What really blew me away was how cohesive and creative the whole experience was. I’ve eaten at a fair number of great restaurants, but Em stood out in a way that felt personal and special. It’s one of those places where you can feel the intention behind every detail. And now that I’ve seen Em featured on the Apple TV show Knife Edge, I’m even more excited. This time, I booked the kitchen counter seats—I’ll be right there watching the chefs while they create everything. It honestly feels like a dream dinner. Em is easily one of the top dining experiences in Mexico City for me, and I can’t wait to come back and share it with my husband.

I‘ve got invited for a dinner in Em an really loved it. Everything was perfect from A-Z. Service was incredible friendly and attentive (I‘m really picky tbh). All the dishes were incredible both visually and in terms of taste. The day before we ate at another 1 start restaurant and this one was definitely on another level. I will come back soon and can highly recommend it. TOP🙌🏼🥳😍

reviews.reviewText: The place is beautiful, the vibe is great, and the food? Incredible. I had the Kumiho cocktail—super well made and delicious. We ordered the Korean Fest and loved everything, especially the kimchi soup and the ejotes (seriously, don’t skip those). I also tried two different wines and they were perfectly paired with the food. Didn’t get many photos—just the desserts, which were amazing too. Service was great, super friendly. Definitely a must if you’re in CDMX!

Jowong is the kind of place that has a vibe of its own. Not only is the food absolutely incredible and the staff super friendly, but the atmosphere here is super chill. I visited for their second anniversary, and although the menu was limited, every single dish that I tried was absolutely delicious. We had so much fun and enjoyed every drink and every bite that we cannot wait to come back to try the rest of the menu. 100% would recommend.

We had a wonderful dining experience at Jowong in Mexico City. Seated at a charming outdoor table, we immediately felt welcomed by the warm and friendly service. The cocktails were a standout—refreshing, well-balanced, and creative. I especially recommend the Perillosa—think pisco sour, but elevated with even more depth and flair. Every dish we tried delivered. The crispy corn and green beans were addictive starters, while the Myeolchi & Potato offered a unique, umami-packed bite. The kimchi carbonara was a bold fusion dish that absolutely worked—comforting and packed with flavor. Jowong is a cozy, vibrant spot perfect for great conversation, good energy, and beautifully crafted food. We’ll definitely be back.

Jowong delivers an exceptional Korean fusion experience in a space that’s both warm and thoughtfully designed, with subtle mid-century modern accents that enhance the overall vibe. The highlights of the meal were the marinated cucumbers, crispy corn, and Caesar salad—each dish was beautifully balanced and full of flavor. These were some of the best fusion-style plates I’ve had in recent memory, with each bite offering something new and delicious. The kimchi carbonara and Korean fried chicken were also excellent, both rich and satisfying without being overwhelming. Service was equally impressive—our waiter was kind, attentive, and spoke perfect English, which made for a seamless and welcoming first night in Mexico City. I would highly recommend Jowong to anyone looking for creative, flavorful food in a great atmosphere.
Korean fusion restaurant that received a Bib Gourmand. Had the fried chicken and kimchi carbonara, both were great. Friendly service in a nice setting.

reviews.reviewText: Everything we had was delicious and super fresh. The tuna tostada is insane and a must order. They had run out of lobster so we got the crab roll which was full of flavour and the shrimp and fish tacos were also delicious. The soft serve is exceedingly good and the flan was fanatic. I can’t fault the food - everything we had was bursting with flavour. There was a mess up with our reservation via our hotel but they were very accommodating and managed to seat us. The mezcal house cocktail is also a must order. Very fresh and balanced. Goes really well with the seafood. Love this place !!!!

Exceptional experience. This is going to be on our list every single time we come to CDMX. Great service, attention to detail, and yes- the prices charged are worth it! The shrimp dish is a standout, as are any of the crudo options. We came here before walking to the Luchador match for an elevated dinner experience, and were welcomed without a reservation (but recommended to make one, because we just got lucky)

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ We only stopped in for cocktails before dinner at Martínez, but this place completely captured us. The design alone is breathtaking—every detail, from the materials to the lighting, feels intentional, layered, and transportive. As interior designers, Peter and I are still talking about it days later. The cocktails were exceptional—crafted with precision and presented with the same artistry that defines the space itself. From what we could see coming out of the kitchen, the food looked nothing short of extraordinary. We’re already planning to return, this time for the full experience. Ultramarinos de Mar is a masterclass in atmosphere and taste—proof that beauty and flavor can exist in perfect harmony.

We were visiting for a week in late November and took my mom there for her 81st birthday. While she has dietary restrictions which prevent her from enjoying the spicy foods of her younger years she really enjoyed the meal. The rest of us did not miss out because we also ordered dishes that brought the heat and when able, the restaurant kindly served the sauces on the side. The crudo, tostada, the grilled shrimp and grilled fish were all so good. A highlight was the flan, which made my mom very happy. Would recommend and hope to go back when we are back in town.

Finally tried this upscale seafood restaurant from my list. Very good food, a little cold but incredibly attentive service, and expensive. I would definitely return with a group to try more of the menu. • Crab cake with beurre blanc (5/5) — Phenomenal, one of the best crab cakes I’ve ever had • Tuna tostada (4/5) — Very good, but the flavor of the tuna didn’t compare to Contramar or Mi Compa Chava’s tuna tostadas • Lobster roll (4/5) — Tasty, but not enough lobster flavor, maybe because there was too much mayonnaise. However the brioche roll was fantastic, so buttery, fluffy and toasted • Soft serve with lemon oil (2/5) — Way too sweet, tasted artificial, and not enough sourness from the lemon. I could only eat 3 bites.

reviews.reviewText: We had great tacos here. They are simple, tasty, inexpensive. I think it’s great that Michelin is awarding places like this with stars, rather than only fine dining restaurants. The night we went there was no waiting time, and we were able to stand in the place and eat whilst watching the tacos being made.

So....we had to try El Califa de León being what I think was the first Michelin stared taco shop. I will say, it's a cool experience, and the tacos were fresh and tasty.... BUT, I really don't think you need to make a special trip there if you are not near by. It was easy to take the metro, but the area, is basically a "local" area, not much around for a tourist, so I wouldnt return. We got 2 of everything except the Nopal which we did not try. We didn't need to order 2 of everything as each order the meat was split between 2 tortillas. It was just meat in tortilla, then there was 2 bowls of salsa. The salsas were really good...particularly the green one. The meats looked very similar, so I don't know which was which. As for the price, it's still mexico so it was cheaper than anything in the US, but kinda expensive for mexico. Also, no place to sit for anyone. There are so many taco shops everywhere, that we felt were much better, and cheaper. I wouldnt return but am glad that we went....if you are looking for that michelin star taco experience there are like 30+ others I'd try next time. If you are looking for the "first", dint over hype yourself or you will be let down

Good street tacos, but not star-worthy. After hearing all the controversy, my friend and I decided to check it out ourselves after working through quite a few of the city’s famous taco spots. We arrived around 7pm on a Tuesday with about ten groups ahead of us. The line didn’t look bad, but it still took roughly 45 minutes to get our order. The setup was simple. One person on the grill, one woman pressing tortillas from fresh dough and tossing them onto the comal. It was very bare-bones, and hygiene didn’t seem like a priority, though at least there weren’t flies hovering around the stand. If you opt to sit inside the neighboring store instead of eating at the standing counters, there’s a mandatory tip (which felt a bit odd). We ordered one of each (Costilla, Bistec, Gaonera, and Chuleta). The larger cuts (Costilla and Chuleta) came sliced across two tortillas, so portions were more generous than we expected. Chuleta and Gaonera were both lean, and since everything is grilled in batches, they came out dry and slightly overcooked. On the other hand, Costilla came with a fat cap intact, which made it juicier and more satisfying even without much garnish. Salsas were limited to a green tomatillo and a roasted chili salsa at each table. We all have decent spice tolerance, but that tomatillo salsa was super sharp and punchy. The roasted chili had better balance. Still think the star felt more like a symbolic gesture from Michelin, but the tacos overall were solid. Not better than other famous taco spots I’ve tried, but the costilla tacos were one of the best versions I’ve had so far in the city.

Few very simple but tasty tacos in this Michelin star taqueria. We went around 4pm and there was no waiting time, we ordered and a few minutes later the.tacos were ready. The tacos come only with meat and then you have two different salsas on your table to add on top. The quality of the meat was great and considering they had some lean meat options like steak and fillet, it was cooked well without being dry.

Taquería El Califa de León is known for being the only taquería in Mexico City awarded a Michelin star, so expectations are understandably high. The quality of the meat is good and the tacos are well executed, but for me, the overall flavour didn’t quite live up to the hype. The tacos were enjoyable, yet not particularly memorable, and the salsas — which are often the star of a great taquería — were underwhelming. Given the price point, it feels more geared toward visitors looking to experience a Michelin-starred taquería rather than locals seeking exceptional flavour. It’s a solid taco experience, but personally, I wouldn’t go out of my way to return.

reviews.reviewText: Had the escargots, char kway teow, siew yok and lettuce and they were all good. Considering there might be asian ingredient limitations in CDMX, I reckon that the taste was as authentic to Singaporean flavours as possible. If there's a constructive criticism to be made, I felt that that the staff seemed a little stone-faced and low in morale. But other than that everything's good! Give it try when you're in CDMX!

I want to say first that the service was excellent. We were taken care from the second we walked in the door. But the food left a lot to be desired. We started with a shrimp curry which was delicious. Then ordered what we thought would be a mix of green vegetables, but turned out to be just a bowl of lettuce in soy sauce. We also ordered the fish which was more bone than fish. Both dishes were extremely disappointing. Also, they kind of run a scam where they offer you a bottle of water with or without gas to start, then you’re charged $160 pesos, once the water is finished they give you free water. Why not just give free water from the start? Lastly the Music was so loud, at times I couldn’t hear what our server was saying. I feel bad because I was really looking forward to eating here after living a year in southeast Asia I was hoping for something similar.

My friend had made a reservation for Makan on a Friday night- I’ve never been to a Singaporean restaurant so I was interested in trying it. When we got there, it wasn’t very busy. We got some cocktails to start, out of the 3 we got, I think the Lychee Martini tasted the best. We ordered several food items such as the Escargots XO which came with milk bread, the Lak Sa, the chili crab, and Siew Yok. Everything we had was good, but nothing really blew my mind. The service was good too, but also not the best service I’ve ever had. Overall, considering the price and the flavor of the food we had, Makan was a nice dining experience, but not super memorable in my opinion.

First time here as I’m curious how a Singapore restaurant is like in Mexico, they the beverages and wine menu but the food menu I had to go onto their website to view, didn’t quite understand why. Of all dishes I ordered, the laksa was the best, and the chicken rice was a let down, they should have either steam or roasted chicken but it’s something else, mine also took 30 minutes to come not sure why chicken rice takes so long to prepare when the meat was already hanging on the shelf. The chili crab was nice in the sense that you don’t really have to peel it, but the taste was somehow a little too sweet.

we ordered an array of dishes and ate family style & i think this is the way to go with the type of food served here. we each ordered the lychee martini as well & can all confidently say it was one of the best we’ve had. the lychee itself tasted fresh, and not out of the can like in so many other establishments. we had a wonderful time here!

reviews.reviewText: This was hands down the best food decision we made during our entire trip. The restaurant itself is beautiful, with a vibe that pulls you in the moment you walk through the door. There are so many gorgeous rooms and little corners that you kind of get lost in it in the best way. And the food. Every single dish we ordered was incredible — honestly, not a single miss. Everything was packed with flavor and beautifully put together. If (when) I come back to Mexico City, I’m planning at least three meals here. No joke. We went around midday and got a table without a problem, but I wouldn’t be surprised if it gets busy during peak hours. Just go. You won’t regret it.

I had an amazing experience dining at this Mediterranean restaurant in Mexico City! The building itself, constructed in the early 1900s, is stunning and full of charm. The old-style design has been beautifully preserved, with candles everywhere creating a cozy and relaxing atmosphere. The décor is tasteful and warm, making the whole place feel incredibly inviting. The menu is small but carefully curated, offering delicious Mediterranean dishes packed with flavor. The cocktail selection is fantastic, every drink we tried was perfectly crafted and absolutely delicious. Overall, this restaurant is a perfect mix of history, ambiance, and incredible food. It’s the kind of spot where you can truly unwind and enjoy an intimate, cozy dining experience. Highly recommend!

The place is very interesting, the atmosphere is great. But I have many questions for the restaurant staff. For an important dinner, I arrived at the restaurant a few days in advance to select a specific table with a beautiful view for the occasion. I was promised that this particular table would be available. However, when we arrived for dinner, our table was occupied by another group. The hostess explained that the ladies had arrived earlier and simply hadn't vacated the table in time. How is this possible in a restaurant of such a supposedly high standard? They offered us another, smaller table with a different view, which really upset me. The dinner was already ruined by this incident; it's disrespectful to the guests. Advice for the restaurant: if you have a reservation for a specific table, you need to warn guests about the time limit, and that's it! The dishes are overpriced, the portions are small. The only dishes I liked were the burrata salad and the lemon cake.

Taverna in Juárez, CDMX is an excellent place for anyone looking for authentic Mediterranean food in Mexico City. The restaurant is located on Calle General Prim, right in the Cuauhtémoc / Juárez area, and it has a very welcoming, relaxed atmosphere. The food quality is outstanding — fresh ingredients, well-balanced flavors, and dishes that feel genuinely Mediterranean rather than adapted. The pasta and shared plates were especially impressive, and everything arrived perfectly prepared and well presented. Service was professional, attentive, and friendly, without being rushed. The staff knows the menu well and gives good recommendations, which really improves the dining experience. The space itself is clean, comfortable, and ideal for both casual dinners and special occasions. If you’re searching on Google Maps for a great restaurant in Juárez CDMX, Taverna is a solid choice. I would definitely come back and recommend it to anyone looking for high-quality food and excellent service in central Mexico City.

Good little Greek spot with tasty food — we got the fish, and it was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Every dish we saw looked amazing, and the portions were generous. The dinner lights and gorgeous decorations created such a warm and inviting atmosphere, making it a perfect spot for a relaxed meal. Even though there was a line, it moved quickly (about 10 minutes), and the staff were friendly and attentive. Overall, a fantastic dining experience — would definitely come back and recommend to anyone looking for great Greek food!

reviews.reviewText: This was one of my favorite tasting menus. A lot of times tasting menus take too long and the amount of food is overwhelming. This one was perfect. The entire experience was less than two hours and the perfect amount of food. The food was unique and delicious. My favorite courses were the fish and the blue cheese ice cream. The service was excellent. Raymundo was very knowledgeable. I also enjoyed the atmosphere. It's modern but cozy and warm. If we come back to Mexico City, we will certainly come here again. Unfortunately, I was too busy enjoying the food and forgot to take pictures. I did take a picture of the view.

We have eaten at many of the best spots in NYC and abroad and Bajel is at that top tier in every way. +1 on the speed of service and sane portion size. The staff (Ray, Marcos, Nancy, Dafne, Ramses, and Ivais) were perfectly lovely and attentive. The dishes were executed brilliantly and I really enjoyed learning more about Mexican cuisine. The octopus, white mole, kanpachi, and pumpkin dessert were standouts. Bravo!!!

Such a lovely experience! Food - Ordered one vegetarian and two standard tasting menus. Enjoyed the unique courses and pacing of service. Showcased technique and flavors. Vegetarian in the group enjoyed their experience, which is difficult sometimes Service - everyone was so welcoming and helpful! Excellent explanations of Mexican cuisine flavors and ingredients during service. Nancy, Ramses, Dafne etc were so nice Ambiance - felt special and upscale but warm and welcoming. Good for couples or groups. Overall would recommend

This was the best tasting menu I’ve had in a while. Each course was so thoughtfully put together. Just when I thought it couldn’t get better the next course would blow my mind. The service was also impeccable and the restaurant gives you a great view of the city.

A Magical Anniversary Dinner at Bajel, Mexico City From the moment we walked in, the ambiance was elegant yet inviting—with a sophisticated, modern aesthetic and breathtaking views that set the tone for a truly memorable evening. The service, Coyo, Nancy, Marcos, Roy, Ram and Dafne, were all impeccable—warm, attentive, and thoughtful without ever being overbearing. The staff even surprised us with a special touch for our celebration, which made the night feel even more personal and meaningful. And the food? Absolutely exquisite. Every dish was a creative, flavor-packed work of art. The ingredients were fresh, the presentation stunning, and the flavors perfectly balanced. The cocktail menu was equally impressive—bold, refined, and delicious. Bajel isn’t just a restaurant—it’s an experience. It’s clear that every detail is curated with care, from the menu to the lighting to the service. We left feeling full, happy, and deeply grateful for such a magical evening. If you're celebrating something special—or just want a night to remember—Bajel is the place. My only complaint is that my stomach was just not big enough.

reviews.reviewText: Voraz is truly a restaurant that innovates in gastronomy, however, there were some details they missed to be outstanding. Overall is it is great. The menu sets a proposal for modern Mexican cuisine that offers a fantastic mix of flavors and techniques. But some plates and ingredients fell short to that potential. The service is great, and the restaurant is very well set up on a place that keeps a traditional mood of the city. The tamale was the best dish, it went beyond traditions and brought a new set of textures while keeping the authentic Mexican taste.

First time here and we were delighted. It was delicious! Favorite dish was the tostada de atun con salsa matcha. We also loved the broccoli. Outstanding. They offered a savory churro that was wonderful. They had a salad with beef- we requested more lettuce and less beef. Amazing.wings had amazing flavor (a little tough though) and delicious house made ranch. Great cocktails too! Only downside was our server was a bit absent at the end, which didn’t match the service we had at the onset.

Everything we ordered was top notch - wings, arrachera, broccoli and the mushroom special. The food is bold and creative and the cocktails are fantastic. The space is effortlessly cool and the music perfect for a lively Friday night. The staff made an extra special effort for my partner’s birthday. A perfect spot for an elevated night out!

Our favourite meal in CDMX. We loved it so much, we had to come back again before we left. All the food was incredible, and the salsas were next level. Our favourite dishes: green ceviche, taco McAllen, wings and the savoury churro.

Voraz was a wonderful experience on my first night in Mexico City. The ambiance, dim and modern, was inviting. I was greeted by Valerie and sat at the bar. I had the arrachera mixteca which was cooked perfectly and layered on top of a rich sauce. The margarita santa is the most unique margarita i’ve had, it’s made in a tall glass (pictured), has floral notes and is presented beautifully. The bartender was amazing! They do have outdoor seating available!

restaurants.name: LINA
restaurants.generatedDescription: LINA, located in Mexico City's Roma neighborhood, is a highly anticipated addition to the dining scene. Guided by chef Mariana Villegas, who honed her skills at Pujol under the renowned chef Enrique Olvera, this restaurant offers a delightful atmosphere from the moment you enter. The long candlelit hallway leads to a main dining room and a charming patio with a central fountain. Guests have shared mixed reviews about their experiences at LINA.
restaurants.address: Av. Yucatán 147, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: LINA, located in Mexico City's Roma neighborhood, has garnered rave reviews for its locally sourced ingredients and tasteful flavors. Reviewers praised the diverse menu with standout dishes like Stone Crab Pasta and Catch of the day. The attentive staff, innovative combinations, and delightful dining room ambiance were highlighted as key elements of the exceptional experience at Lina.

Enjoy a diverse menu with standout dishes like Stone Crab Pasta and Catch of the day
Experience excellent service from an attentive staff in a beautifully decorated dining room
tips: Make reservations in advance to secure a table at this popular spot
Try multiple dishes to sample a variety of flavors offered on the menu
Consider asking for recommendations from the waiter based on your preferences for an enhanced dining experience
Visit during off-peak hours for a more relaxed atmosphere

reviews.reviewText: So, so excellent. Came here on the recommendation of a friend and loved everything. Such innovative flavors and combinations. The clam and uni dish was unforgettable, the chicken (their specialty) came with an incredible mole, and both desserts were delicious. Great staff and good drinks too.

One of the best meals we had in Mexico City! Each dish was delicious, the wine selection was some of the best we had seen, and the service attentive/friendly. We were a group of 6 and ordered 10 dishes to share, there was something for everyone! The steak and chicken dishes were standouts. Would highly recommend!

What a treat. From the beautiful, simply decorated dining room, to the delightful tableware, everything is so eye pleasing. The staff on the floor was so attentive and kind. Chef Mariana is such a warm, passionate and talented woman. The food was simply delicious. The flavors are wonderful and unexpected, often delicate, sometimes bold. The textures were divine. Thank you for a fantastic dinner ♥️

We tried almost everything from the menu and it was all amazing. My favorite apps were tuna crudo, tartar and cucumber. Also the chicken mole was sooo good! The steak could have been cooked more to medium - but we didn’t say and they didn’t ask. Great experience overall!

Excellent restaurant in CDMX, proposing signature mexican dishes, Michelin style, however much better in terms of quantity and price. The owner is always available and ready to help. The cocktails are really good and creative as well, with niche ingredients. Innovative flavours, local heritage and creative presentation join together for a timeless, sensorial mexican experience.

restaurants.name: Baldío
restaurants.generatedDescription: Baldío proudly claims the title of Mexico City's first "zero waste" restaurant, inspired by London's Silo. This innovative eatery is on a mission to minimize waste as much as possible, showcasing local vegetables, herbs, and fermented ingredients in its menu. Unique touches like ordering on ceramic tiles and cocktails served on tap highlight their commitment to sustainability.
restaurants.address: Antonio Sola 26, Colonia Condesa, Cuauhtémoc, 06140 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Baldío in Mexico City is a hidden gem that offers an exceptional dining experience with great attention to detail, aesthetic, and vibe. Reviewers highly praise the tasting menu, ceviche, esquites, and innovative cuisine showcasing vibrant flavors of locally-sourced produce. The restaurant's dedication to sustainability through eco-friendly practices like regenerative agriculture and zero waste adds a unique touch to the dining experience. Guests appreciate the knowledgeable staff who provide thorough explanations of dishes and wine pairings in English.
reasonsToVisit: Experience a truly authentic and sustainable dining experience at Baldío
Enjoy a diverse selection of seafood, vegetarian, and meat dishes with balanced flavors
Witness the chefs in action while seated at the bar for a front-row view of culinary artistry
Indulge in unique dishes like pan de masa with popcorn butter, smoky esquites, fresh crudo, seasonal fish with black garlic puree
tips: For an immersive experience, sit at the bar to watch the chefs prepare each dish up close
Try their signature cocktails; if you enjoy margaritas, it's a must-try according to reviewers
Consider making reservations in advance as Baldío is popular among locals and tourists alike
Visit during off-peak hours for a more intimate dining atmosphere

reviews.reviewText: This place is very special... you're eating real food, all of it. Basically nothing is wasted... the staff is very warm and helpful when you try to communicate with them. They explained everything in English for us because we knew very little Spanish. We had the tasting menu and it was incredibly delicious... the flavors and ingredients were beautifully put together and tasty, always waiting for the next course to arrive. There's so much in every dish, it's hard to explain to you what was in there... when visiting Mexico City, it's a place you need to stop and eat. Their cocktails were really good too.

We chose this spot for dinner on our last night in CDMX, and I’m so glad we did! What an incredible dining experience from start to finish. The food, décor, atmosphere, service, and presentation were all absolutely perfect. We sat at the counter and loved watching each beautiful plate being prepared. I started with a prickly pear fermented juice, so fresh and delicious. We shared several small plates including the ceviche, chorizo, esquites, and pumpkin, and each dish somehow topped the last. By the time we finished, we were full but couldn’t resist ordering double dessert instead of a main, and they were just as outstanding. If you have the chance to eat here, don’t miss it. I’m sure you can’t go wrong with anything on the menu!

Baldío is my new favorite restaurant in CDMX! We went with friends to celebrate our birthdays, and the entire experience was unforgettable from start to finish. We arrived late for our reservation, but the staff was incredibly kind and still seated us without any issue. When they found out we were celebrating, they surprised us with complimentary wine and dessert — such a kind, thoughtful gesture that made us feel really taken care of. The food was phenomenal — elevated Mexican cuisine with so much flavor and attention to detail in every dish. One of our friends has a nut allergy, and they made sure everything was prepared safely, which we really appreciated. We mentioned it was our last night in the city, and they wouldn’t let us leave without sharing their favorite local bar recommendations. True hospitality. 10/10 — no notes. Can’t wait to come back!

We were very surprised by the Kale and the vegetables. Both dishes appeared to be simple but were finely elevated. We also had the pork with mole tacos, which had some Korean inspiration and was absolutely great. Overall this place is very enjoyable. The food is of great quality and the service is friendly, quick and very attentive. I would definitely recommend for a nice dinner and I cannot wait to be back.

We dined at Baldío twice during our visits to CDMX in July and August, and both experiences were exceptional. Our first visit featured the lunch testing menu, where each course showcased meticulous plating and vibrant, layered flavours. While the savory dishes impressed, the beverage program and desserts truly elevated the meal. The seasonal tepache — a traditional Mexican fermented beverage — deserves special mention. Baldío's creative interpretations, particularly the tamarind and guava variations, deliver a complex interplay of tang, sweetness, and effervescence that feels both rooted in tradition and refreshingly contemporary. The house-made kombucha is equally noteworthy: expertly fermented, well-balanced, and brimming with nuanced flavor. The care in their fermentation process is evident in every sip. We enjoyed our first visit so much that we returned weeks later (no reservation) specifically for drinks and dessert. Seated outside at the open window bar, we savoured both the view into the kitchen, bar and engaging conversation with the knowledgeable team. Once again, the tepache and desserts proved impeccable — the perfect light indulgence for an afternoon. Beyond the exemplary food and beverages, what distinguishes Baldío is its unwavering commitment to zero-waste practices. As one of Mexico City's pioneers in sustainable gastronomy, the restaurant thoughtfully integrates environmental responsibility into every aspect — from ingredient sourcing to final presentation — without sacrificing creativity or quality. It's a rare marriage of culinary innovation and ethical consciousness. Highly recommended for anyone seeking progressive, sustainably-minded cuisine in one of CDMX's most forward-thinking establishments.

restaurants.name: Propio
restaurants.generatedDescription: Nestled in a vibrant area, Propio offers an inviting dining experience reminiscent of traditional restaurants, complete with a spacious layout and attentive staff. The front hall captivates with its lush greenery against frosted glass windows, evoking the charm of East Asian art. The contemporary Mexican menu features delightful dishes like pork tacos with mole negro and a refreshing kale salad dressed in yuzu.
restaurants.address: Av. Álvaro Obregón 182, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Propio is a new and spectacular restaurant in Rome with exquisite food, a great atmosphere, and friendly waiters. Reviewers highly recommend the fish, cuts like ribs, starter bread with hazelnut butter, tomato salad, oysters, pork chop, crab croquettes, softshell rice, and more. While some reviewers found the staff pushy about ordering drinks or leaving quickly and felt the place was overrated and overpriced for mediocre cocktails and food; others praised it as the best meal of their trip with incredible dishes like monkey bread and pork belly rib. The ambiance is described as chic yet foodie-friendly with exceptional service.
reasonsToVisit: Exquisite food including spectacular fish dishes
Chic ambiance with a mix of foodie vibes
Friendly waitstaff providing exceptional service
Unique dishes like pork chop, crab croquettes & softshell rice
tips: Try the must-have items such as the pork belly rib and monkey bread when sharing plates
Consider making reservations to avoid waiting times due to popularity
Visit during weekdays for potentially quieter dining experiences compared to weekends
Explore other nearby attractions after dining at Propio for a complete experience

reviews.reviewText: I’ve tried over 150 restaurants in CDMX and Propio is one of my favorites. Skip the desserts because they’re forgettable, but they have several *unmissable* appetizers & main courses. • The parker house rolls with chive butter are addicting and possibly the best bread dish in the city. • The red rice is rich, savory, sour, and phenomenal. • The “bacon rib” is spectacular and the richness is perfectly complemented by the mustard glaze. Order it with tortillas. • The chicken with huitlacoche orzo and chimichurri is so flavorful that it made up for slightly dry chicken. Don’t miss it.

Amazing experience, very attentive staff. The Food is just great. Had the Parker House Rolls, which are an amazong Brioche bread with Butter. Then the Jitomates which were good. The Rib Eye was perfect. Can really recommend this restaurant as it stands out among others

Upon arrival, I was notified that the restaurant had no power but they had a generator truck out front trying to restore power. We were led to the back patio area to wait and provided complementary beverages. Power was restored not long after and we were led to our table. There were some gas fumes from the generator but the staff was very accommodating despite working through difficult circumstances. Despite all the issues, the food and drinks were great! Service was solid despite all that was going on. The space itself was beautifully designed and divided into 3 distinct sections. The bacon rib and sea bass were excellent but the soft shell crab with red rice was my absolute standout. The "vuelve la vida" and tomato dishes were also delicious. I wish they were more upfront about the extra service fee which they called a tax (but the menu said prices are inclusive of tax already) but that's really a minor gripe about an otherwise superb dining establishment. I would be very surprised if Propio does not get a star in the coming years.
Delicious good and great service! I loved the cocktails, Parker House rolls, kale salad, grilled chicken, and ribeye. Fantastic!

Great vibes and fabulous food. Everything we ordered was amazing. Food was slightly colder than desirable but flavor made up for it. Also, found it a bit annoying that the servers kept removing things from the table while we were still eating but I guess this might be typical of service in Mexico? Overall a real treat 🌟

The chef pays special attention to vegetarian dishes, making it a great option for those who appreciate well-prepared vegetables. Despite its small size, the restaurant offers a quiet atmosphere and high-quality ingredients, which contribute to its slightly higher prices. Visitors praise the flavorful food, attractive presentation, and overall pleasant dining experience at Fugaz.
restaurants.address: C. Orizaba 3-3 B, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Fugaz is a charming and inventive restaurant in Mexico City that offers small plates with great flavors, exceptional service, and a unique fusion of Mexican and Asian cuisines. Reviewers praise the delicious dishes like avocado tostadas, shrimp pita with yellow mole, and tartare sandwich. The wine selection is well thought out, and the atmosphere is described as chill and relaxed. Enjoy exceptional service in a beautiful and charming setting
Try skillfully selected wines alongside creative cocktails
tips: Make reservations via Instagram due to limited seating
Visit during lunch or dinner from Thursday to Sunday when Fugaz is open
Try seasonal rotating menu items for fresh experiences

reviews.reviewText: This place has some cool vibes and very unique fusion food. A mixture between Asian and Mexican. We had the tartare sandwich and the tostada de camaron. Both were very good and delicious. The flavors went very well together. The staff was very nice and attentive and was very quick on the water service among other things. The atmosphere is very chill and relaxed and lots of cool wall and shelf items you can observe.

Really enjoyed the food here and the service was lovely. All of the food had a light touch with great flavours. Unfortunately for me the portions are small plates so if your a big eater you need a lot of cash. Clearly tailored and priced for tourists that being said well worth a visit.

I finally made it to Fugaz for lunch today after a failed attempt 2 mos ago. Had the shrimp tostada which was good but had 2 other dishes which were pretty bad - the leek goat cheese peach dish which had so many divergent elements to the dish that it was almost inedible. Lastly I tried the venison tartare that the server recommended- I love tartare but this one was so over salted I could barely eat it. Ofc I did finish it bc I paid for it lol but truly disappointed w my experience today. Maybe just an off day…

Wonderful, tiny restaurant with delicious & inventive food & drinks. The dishes are small, but reasonably priced for such a high quality restaurant. Heavy on unusual fish dishes, including cured tuna. The shrimp pita with yellow mole was delicious. Panela with mezcal also highly recommended. This place is great.
Food was absolutely delicious - my favorite dish was the sole. The staff and ambiance are cool and very friendly, restaurant has a chill vibe with great music. Would absolutely come back!

restaurants.name: Galea
restaurants.generatedDescription: Galea, a restaurant located in CDMX, has garnered much praise for its delectable dishes and inviting ambiance. Visitors have raved about the diverse menu offerings, from mouthwatering pasta dishes to delightful vegan options. The friendly staff and cozy atmosphere add to the overall dining experience. Guests have particularly enjoyed the homemade bread and expertly crafted cocktails at the bar.
restaurants.address: Sinaloa 67, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX, Mexico
restaurants.reviewsSummary: Galea is a hidden gem for fine dining in Mexico City, known for its exceptional Italian cuisine and cozy atmosphere. Reviewers rave about the phenomenal food, with standout dishes like the melt-in-your-mouth fish, octopus appetizer, and homemade pastas. The restaurant offers a concise menu with seasonal specials and prompt service. Guests praise the flavorful pastas made in-house and recommend trying multiple dishes by opting for half portions.
